<!-- @slot inventory-rows -->
| C-HC-01 | The spec's PHI inventory lists every PHI element, and the data model's PHI classification matches it field for field (HIPAA §164.502(b)). | [ ] | |
| C-HC-02 | Each element is marked with its Safe Harbor identifier type, or as health data (HIPAA §164.514(b)(2)). | [ ] | |
| C-HC-03 | The project's role is recorded: covered entity, business associate, or neither (HIPAA §164.502(a)). | [ ] | |

<!-- @slot minimisation-rows -->
| C-HC-04 | Each role sees only the PHI its work needs, and each routine disclosure sends only the elements its purpose needs (HIPAA §164.502(b), §164.514(d)). | [ ] | |
| C-HC-05 | Non-production data is synthetic, or is de-identified by Safe Harbor or Expert Determination, and a check proves it (HIPAA §164.514(a)–(b)). | [ ] | |
| C-HC-06 | Retired media, stores and backups that held PHI are made unreadable, and the plan names the method (HIPAA §164.310(d)(2)(i)). | [ ] | |

<!-- @slot rights-rows -->
| C-HC-07 | A patient can obtain a copy of their record in the form the plan states, within the time limit (HIPAA §164.524). | [ ] | |
| C-HC-08 | A correction is recorded as an amendment, and the original stays retrievable (HIPAA §164.526). | [ ] | |
| C-HC-09 | Disclosures that a patient may ask to see are recorded so that an accounting can be produced (HIPAA §164.528). | [ ] | |
| C-HC-10 | A use or disclosure that needs the patient's authorisation is blocked until one is recorded (HIPAA §164.508). | [ ] | |

<!-- @slot sharing-rows -->
| C-HC-11 | Each recipient of PHI is a permitted disclosure, or a business associate with a signed agreement (HIPAA §164.502(e), §164.504(e)). | [ ] | |
| C-HC-12 | No PHI is sent to an AI model, an analytics service or a support tool that the agreement register does not cover (HIPAA §164.502(e)). | [ ] | |
| C-HC-13 | The breach runbook names who assesses an incident and who notifies, within the rule's time limits (HIPAA §164.402, §164.404, §164.410). | [ ] | |
